claims.statement: The EU In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation requires performance evidence and addresses metrological traceability of calibrator and control-material values, underscoring that measurement method and traceability matter when interpreting laboratory results.

Hypothesis: preventive-health clinics lose time and confidence when longitudinal panels arrive in inconsistent units, ranges, and assay contexts, and will pay for normalized display with explicit comparability warnings rather than a diagnostic conclusion.

contrary_evidence: Laboratory information systems already normalize many units and ranges inside a single provider.
For some analytes, method changes are too complex for a general comparability score and should simply be flagged as non-comparable.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: provide a synthetic-data sandbox to two clinic-software vendors, then charge when normalization is embedded in the patient timeline.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 3 integrations in year 2, 15 in year 4, and 40 Central European platforms in year 6 at 200000 PLN average annual revenue produces 8M PLN ARR. At 4-6x ARR and 55-70% founder ownership, the founder can exceed 5M PLN equity if regulatory scope remains manageable and integration retention is proven.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours/week for mapping and pilot management, with clinical and privacy specialists contracted for bounded reviews.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 80-88% after OCR/API processing, terminology maintenance, security, and clinical review sampling.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 7-12 months at 15000-30000 PLN integration-led acquisition cost and 3000-8000 PLN monthly revenue per platform.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 2-6 PLN per normalized panel with 1000-5000 PLN monthly minimums for clinic-software integrations.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: every follow-up panel repeats the workflow; retention becomes strong after API embedding and accumulated patient provenance.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consent-based cross-lab transition pairs, assay metadata mappings, and clinician-reviewed comparability exceptions
fingerprint.customer: Polish preventive-health, longevity, and telemedicine clinics receiving external laboratory results
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Integrations with clinic portals, LIS/EHR vendors, and private lab import workflows
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Unit/range/method normalization, provenance-preserving trend display, and comparability warnings as embedded B2B API
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Clinic software vendor or clinic pays per normalized panel or monthly API volume tier
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A patient imports a new panel from a different laboratory, assay, or reporting format

founder_fit: Direct fit with health data, statistical comparability, and quantified-self interests.
Medical-student partner can help identify workflow questions without replacing qualified regulatory or clinical advice.
API model is asynchronous and scalable rather than consultation-heavy.
Can validate using synthetic panels and public reference documentation before processing patient data.
risks: A misleading normalized trend could influence care; original values, method warnings, and clinician review must be preserved.
Special-category health data create severe privacy and breach consequences.
Labs may not expose assay/platform metadata in machine-readable form.

structure.control_point: assay-aware longitudinal provenance and comparability mapping embedded in clinic timelines
structure.critical_dependency: complete method metadata and a legally validated non-diagnostic product boundary

thesis: A non-diagnostic API for Polish preventive-health clinics that preserves assay, unit, reference-range, specimen, and timing context when patients bring results from multiple laboratories. Consent-based transition data can eventually quantify when apparent biomarker changes reflect method changes rather than physiology.
title: LabBridge Longitudinal Result Normalization API
uncertainties: Medical-device classification depends on intended use and claims; the first version must remain administrative and non-diagnostic unless properly validated.
Clinics' data-controller roles, consent flows, and cross-lab metadata completeness need legal and technical validation.
The 80000 PLN capital estimate and all commercial figures below are planning hypotheses.
